doc.title: A.B. Spellman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 19, 2022

title: Revision, scansion and punctuation in his poetry
summary: He revises heavily, hears lines, uses iambics, and avoids capitals and heavy punctuation.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: That’s marvelous. Thank you very much. I’m going to use a term you used to describe a Cannonball Adderley solo. It was perfect, not a wrong note.
Thank you. Yeah, well, I revise a lot. I try to be sure that every word is the right word. A lot of people don’t like revision. I think that for poetry I don’t think that there are — I’ve

only known maybe two people in my life who could write a poem without revision and it would be worthy of publication. And I even thought that those poems would have improved if they had sat down and gone over and changed a thing here and there.
When you’re considering revisions do you read it aloud?

I hear it, yeah, I definitely hear it. And I use a lot of iambics not because — it’s not an intentional matter I don’t have any particular brief for iambics except that the lines have to scan for me. They have to scan. And they have to swing a little bit. And I think iambics help me do that.

There are decisions you and other poets make regarding uppercase letters. And I’m looking at the poem and there’s no uppercase. And I’ve wondered in the past, what is the — is there a reason for that?

I used to have one and it had to involve the diminution of the ego and of the — having more poetry of equality where everything stood at the same level. I got used to me having that it’s nice, but the fact is I just do it because I’ve always done it. And I try to punctuate with measure. I very seldom — I punctuate when I can’t get out of it. Question marks for example, I can’t find a way around, but usually I try to punctuate at the end of the line on the page would be where the period would be. And I sometimes like to have, I like to have words bump into each other without commas or semicolons or the like interrupting them. I think you can find more things in the relationship with the words I think without punctuation being there. Not everybody agrees with that approach. But it’s fairly common nowadays. I used to be, you know, sort of out there by doing it but now I see it all the time.
